note: Atomic tasks for the DSS research line only. Framework work (crates, phases) is tracked in /docs/STATUS.md, not here. Each task states what would count as done, because 'investigate X' is not a task anyone can finish.

tasks.title: Make DSS's deviation reference robust
tasks.why: The last unresolved cause of a measured DSS failure. §5.8.1 isolated it: DSS measures every client's deviation against `base.aggregate(updates)`, and when the base is fragile (fedavg) a lone attacker drags that reference around every round, so every honest client's trace becomes volatile too and every collusion score saturates near ceiling (measured 0.999998 across 9 honest clients). The clients aren't misbehaving; the yardstick is.
tasks.approach: Decouple the reference from the base method: compute it with a robust statistic (coordinate-wise median or a trimmed mean over the batch) regardless of which base is being wrapped. The base method would then inform only the combine step, which is where §5.11 already moved it. Costs one extra reduction per round.
tasks.done_when: Experiment 2.6 re-run shows dss_fedavg vs solo adaptive_evasion materially below its current 36.34, with the honest-client collusion saturation in run_dss_diagnostics dropping well below 0.999. If it doesn't move, that is also a finding -- write it up.

tasks.title: Decide the stability/collusion combination rule
tasks.why: §5.12 established the AND-gate is trading away something real: collusion-only scores 1.09 against non-identical stable colluders where stability-only scores 17.13 (no better than undefended fedavg). The gate's conservatism has a measured cost.
tasks.approach: Do NOT simply flip to OR. The AND-gate exists to protect legitimately-noisy honest clients from being penalized for instability alone -- Claim 2's problem, which §5.4 measured as real. §5.12's scenario contains no non-IID minority, so it cannot see that cost. First run the ablation against the §5.4 fairness scenario WITH a non-IID minority present; then decide between AND, OR, and a weighted combination.
tasks.done_when: A fairness-scenario ablation exists (stability-only vs collusion-only vs AND, with a non-IID minority and no attackers), and the combination rule is either changed with evidence or documented as deliberately conservative with the measured cost stated.
blocked_by: user decision on whether to change a mechanism §6.1 defined
tasks.notes: UNBLOCKED 2026-09-01 (section 5.15). The blocker was never the experiment: run_fairness_experiment.rs called build_aggregator directly (so no dss_ name resolved) and was single-round (so DSS's gate could not fire — stability returns 1.0 below two trace entries). Both fixed; Experiment 2.11 ran 6,720 rows, 20 seeds, 20 rounds, zero attackers. RESULT: dropping the stability conjunct does NOT reopen Claim 2. Collusion-only DSS scores 1.030 +/- 0.177 minority/majority influence at the widest shift — a CI containing 1.0, i.e. parity — while krum (0.636) and flanders_krum (0.746) both down-weight the minority. The shipped gate returns fedavg's numbers exactly and buys no fairness the collusion-only variant lacks. The objection is removed; the decision to change DSS's default is the project owner's and has NOT been made here. Thresholds unchanged.

tasks.title: Fix or document the centered_clipping default
tasks.why: §5.13: at the shipped default clip_radius=1.0, Centered Clipping scored 0.078 on poisoned MNIST -- worse than no defense (fedavg 0.163) and far below krum (0.844). A sweep 1->5->20->100 rises monotonically toward FedAvg with no optimum. The default is a placeholder that a deployment could reasonably mistake for a recommendation.
tasks.approach: Two options, not exclusive. (a) Document loudly: the config field's doc comment and USAGE.md say tau MUST be tuned to the model's weight scale, with §5.13's numbers as the warning. (b) Investigate a dimension-aware default, e.g. scaling tau by sqrt(dim) or by the observed inter-client deviation norm -- but that would deviate from Karimireddy et al., so it needs ADR 0008 justification or must live behind an explicit opt-in.
tasks.done_when: Either the default is changed with a cited justification, or clip_radius's documentation states the failure mode and the measured numbers in the places an operator would actually look (config doc comment, USAGE.md, aggregation-catalog).

tasks.title: Multi-seed the real-data validation
tasks.why: §5.13 is one seed per cell. That is adequate for its negative result about clip_radius (a default losing to no-defense at every tested tau doesn't need many seeds) but not for the comparative krum/trimmed_mean claims, which are currently corroboration rather than evidence.
tasks.approach: benchmark.py already sweeps (aggregator x split x attack); it needs a --seeds dimension, and run_demo.sh needs to thread a seed through partition_data.py. Then 5 seeds over the existing grid.
tasks.done_when: Experiment 3.1 re-run with >=5 seeds per cell and confidence intervals in the summary, matching §7.3's discipline for the synthetic experiments.
tasks.notes: Half done 2026-09-01. run_demo.sh gained CONFLUX_DEMO_SEED, and section 5.16.1 used it for a 3-seed check of the headline comparison. But it seeds the DATA PARTITION ONLY -- the trainer clients keep their own uncontrolled randomness, discovered by the same nominal seed 42 giving krum 0.655 in 5.16 and 0.718 in 5.16.1. That 0.063 spread is a useful free measurement of harness variance (the finding's gap is 9.1x larger), but full reproducibility needs the trainers seeded too, and benchmark.py still does not expose the seed at all.

tasks.title: Run the non-IID and adaptive-attack cells on real data
tasks.why: §5.13 covers IID + one persistent Byzantine attacker. The findings most at risk of not transferring are the non-IID fairness result (§5.4) and the adaptive-attacker results (§5.7) -- neither has been checked against a real model.
tasks.approach: No new code: benchmark.py already accepts --splits dirichlet:<alpha>, and e2e_pytorch_shakespeare provides a NATURAL non-IID partition (one client per speaking role) that doesn't depend on a synthetic knob at all. This is runs, not redesign.
tasks.done_when: A results file covering (>=2 aggregators x IID vs non-IID x attack/no-attack) on at least MNIST and Shakespeare, written up as a §5.13 successor.

tasks.title: Report FoolsGold's degradation against non-identical colluders
tasks.why: §5.12 found FoolsGold drops 1.35 -> 9.93 (5.6x) when colluders share an objective but not a byte stream. This is a limitation of a published method under a threat model its own paper doesn't test, found incidentally. It is currently one paragraph inside a section about something else.
tasks.approach: Either promote it to its own experiment with a divergence sweep (0.0 -> identical, through to fully independent), or explicitly scope it as an observation not a claim. A sweep would establish whether the degradation is gradual or has a threshold.
tasks.done_when: Either a divergence-sweep experiment exists, or §5.12 states plainly that the single divergence value tested makes this an observation rather than a characterization.

tasks.title: FEMNIST harness
tasks.why: Deliberately deferred, with a concrete obstacle rather than a vague 'expensive'. FEMNIST's value is its partition BY WRITER IDENTITY, and torchvision's EMNIST distribution ships the images without writer labels -- so building it from there would produce another synthetic partition, defeating the entire point. A faithful version needs LEAF's preprocessing pipeline over raw NIST Special Database 19 (several GB, multi-stage).
tasks.approach: Only worth doing if a second naturally-partitioned dataset is needed. e2e_pytorch_shakespeare already provides one.
tasks.done_when: n/a -- revisit only if Shakespeare proves insufficient.
blocked_by: cost/benefit -- reconsider only if a second natural partition is needed

tasks.title: Decide whether DSS is going toward publication
tasks.why: §6.5 already positions DSS against the closest prior art (FoolsGold, Centered Clipping, FLTrust/Zeno) and concludes it is a genuine but narrow contribution -- a specific synthesis of existing ideas, not a new primitive. Whether that clears a venue's bar is a judgment call nobody has made, and it determines whether p2/p3 are worth any effort.
tasks.done_when: A decision is recorded in PROGRESS.json.

tasks.title: Consolidate figures for the results narrative
tasks.why: docs/research/figures/ exists but the strongest results (§5.11's Finding 3 repair, §5.12's ablation separation, §5.13's tau curve) are tables only. The Finding-3 before/after in particular is a single memorable chart.
tasks.done_when: At least the three named results have plots generated by a committed script, not by hand.

tasks.title: Extract a standalone results narrative
tasks.why: temporal-consistency-aggregation.md is now ~1,700 lines and interleaves hypothesis, method, thirteen experiments, and running self-correction. That structure is excellent as a lab notebook and wrong for a reader who wants the result.
tasks.approach: Do not restructure the notebook -- its chronology is what makes the self-corrections legible. Extract a separate short document that states the claims and points into it.
tasks.done_when: A standalone summary exists that a reader can finish in ten minutes.

tasks.title: Re-run the FLANDERS comparison on a real model
tasks.why: Section 5.14 is entirely at dim=3. FLANDERS's cost and signal both scale with model dimension in a way DSS's scalar traces do not, so the comparison that most favours DSS is also the one least tested at scale. Section 5.13 is the standing caution.
tasks.how: benchmark.py against e2e_pytorch_mnist, aggregators dss_fedavg / flanders_krum / krum, >=5 seeds.
tasks.notes: Done 2026-09-01 (section 5.16). Running FLANDERS on a real model first OOM-killed the server twice — its MAR matrix is d x d, so 20.7 GB at 50,890 parameters. Fixed with the paper's own 500-coordinate subsampling (8+ GB -> 258 MB). The accuracy result reproduces and strengthens 5.14's Finding 3: undefended, flanders(=FLANDERS+Krum) and krum are indistinguishable (0.671 vs 0.669); under attack krum holds at 0.655 while flanders collapses to 0.102, below undefended fedavg's 0.181. Single-seed; 5.16.1 adds a 3-seed check of that one comparison. STRUCTURAL LIMIT: DSS cannot be measured on real data at all, because the harness drives the real server binary and AGENT.md's rule keeps DSS out of build_aggregator.
